_meta.indication: Treatment of postmenopausal women or adult men with ER-positive, HER2-negative, ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer with disease progression following at least one line of endocrine therapy

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 3 randomized, active-controlled, open-label, multicenter trial
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (1:1) to ORSERDU 345 mg orally once daily (n=239) vs investigator's choice of endocrine therapy (n=239: fulvestrant n=166 or an aromatase inhibitor n=73); stratified by ESR1 mutation status, prior fulvestrant, and visceral metastasis
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer with disease progression following 1-2 prior lines of endocrine therapy, including 1 line containing a CDK4/6 inhibitor
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Progression-free survival (PFS) based on Imaging Review Committee (IRC), tested in the ESR1-mut subpopulation and in the ITT population
pivotal_trials.n: 478 patients randomized in ITT; ESR1-mut subpopulation N=115 (ORSERDU) and N=113 (fulvestrant or AI)
pivotal_trials.result: In the ESR1-mut subpopulation, median PFS 3.8 months (elacestrant) vs 1.9 months (SOC); HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.39-0.77), p=0.0005. In the ITT population, median PFS 2.8 vs 1.9 months; HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.55-0.88), p=0.0018. OS in ESR1-mut HR 0.90 (95% CI 0.63, 1.30), not significant.

key_safety: Most common (>=10%) adverse reactions were musculoskeletal pain (41% vs 39%), nausea (35% vs 19%), increased cholesterol, increased AST, increased triglycerides, fatigue, decreased hemoglobin, vomiting (19% vs 9%), and others. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 12% of patients; fatal adverse reactions in 1.7%. Hypercholesterolemia (30%) and hypertriglyceridemia (27%) occurred.
target_moa: Elacestrant is an oral estrogen receptor antagonist and selective estrogen receptor degrader (SERD); it binds ERalpha with high affinity (IC50 48 nM), antagonizes estradiol-mediated ER-positive breast cancer cell proliferation, and causes down-regulation and degradation of the ER
modality: Small molecule (tetrahydronaphthalene compound; oral estrogen receptor degrader/antagonist)
companion_dx_detail: Patient selection based on presence of ESR1 mutation(s) in plasma specimen using an FDA-approved test

advisory_committee.vote: FDA did not refer this application to an advisory committee as there were no efficacy or safety issues requiring external input
